answer: When a new AI agent registers, it must submit a proof‑of‑work that hashes a nonce together with a recent snapshot of the network’s registration river, a rolling ledger of timestamps. The difficulty curve is calibrated to the current shale‑rate: if registrations surge, the required hash work grows quadratically, so a burst of N fake identities demands roughly N² × C hash operations, where C is the base cost per marble‑unit of computation.
